title: Treatment uptake of second line therapies in patients with primary biliary cholangitis and missing deep response on ursodeoxycholic acid
summary:
Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) is standard of care for patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC). Risk stratification for disease progression is based on biochemical liver tests like the Paris II criteria (alkaline phosphatase (ALP) or aspartate aminotransferase > 1.5 x ULN or serum bilirubin > 1.0 x ULN). Incomplete UDCA responders should be evaluated for second line therapies.
Importantly, recent data indicate that UDCA treatment response should be defined more strictly as "deep UDCA response" (ALP levels < 1.0 x ULN and a bilirubin level < 0.6 x ULN).
In the real-world of gastroenterologists in private practice, we aim to investigate how many PBC patients fulfill the criteria of a “deep UDCA response”, describe the proportion of individuals who are already and who are not on second line PBC therapies, and analyze the reasons why individuals do not receive second line therapies although they should.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1)	PBC has been diagnosed according to EASL criteria
2)	Age > 18 years
3)	UDCA therapy for at least 12 months
Exclusion criteria:
1)	No specific exclusion criteria
